metadata.description: Golden evaluation dataset for MNNIT Robotics Club AI Agent. Contains user-side (read-only) and admin-side (read+write) test cases grounded in real club data.

scoring.tool_selection: Exact match — did the agent pick the correct tool(s)?
scoring.tool_args: Partial match — were the arguments/filters reasonable?
scoring.hallucination_check: Answer must not contain facts absent from source data

test_cases.query: What projects does the robotics club have?
test_cases.expected_answer: The club has multiple projects across categories including the Self-Driving Car (SDC/CART 95), Prosthetic Arm, Robotic Dog, Spider Bot, Humanoid, 5 DOF Robotic Arm, Cleaner Bot, ChatBot, Self Balancing Bot, Smart CCTV Surveillance System, Defect Product Detection, RL in Super Mario Bros, Vision-Guided Rover, and more. Projects span domains like Computer Vision, AI/ML, Inverse Kinematics, Embedded Systems, and ROS.

test_cases.query: Tell me about the self-driving car project. What stage is it at?

club_rag.query: self-driving car SDC CART 95 current status

test_cases.expected_answer: The Self-Driving Car (SDC) project was launched in 2022 and uses a golf cart called CART 95. It has now advanced to phase two development. Key upgrades include switching from a chain drive to a gear-driven steering system, integrating a high-resolution single-turn magnetic encoder with a planetary gear system for accurate steering calibration. The tech stack includes ROS, SLAM, LiDAR, computer vision (lane detection), Carla simulator, and path planning algorithms. The project was featured in Times of India in December 2019.
test_cases.grounding_source: Pragati 2024 pp.12-14, Pragati 2025 pp.14-17, seed-content car-timeline

test_cases.query: Which projects use Arduino?
test_cases.expected_answer: Several projects use Arduino: the Humanoid (bipedal robot with Arduino), Spider Bot (Arduino Nano with Adafruit PWM Servo Driver), Self Balancing Bot (Arduino microcontroller with MPU6050), 5 DOF Robotic Arm (Arduino with servo motors), XY Plotter (Arduino Uno with stepper motors and GRBL firmware), Sign Language Recognizer (Arduino Nano), 6-DOF Robotic Arm (Arduino UNO), and Vision-Guided Rover (Arduino UNO with Jetson Nano).

test_cases.query: What AI/ML projects has the club done? Explain the techniques used.

club_rag.query: AI ML machine learning projects techniques

test_cases.expected_answer: AI/ML projects include: (1) AI Music Generator — uses LSTM neural networks trained on MIDI datasets with PyTorch and Music21, has adjustable temperature and random seed parameters, outputs MIDI/WAV/MP3. (2) Aplytic Resume Analyzer — uses NLP with TF-IDF vectorization, cosine similarity, spaCy, scikit-learn, BERT embeddings, and LanguageToolfor grammar checks; achieves 95% precision in information extraction. (3) Defect Product Detection — uses CNN for quality control in manufacturing. (4) RL in Super Mario Bros — reinforcement learning agent that autonomously plays the game. (5) Smart CCTV Surveillance — uses OpenCV for fire/smoke detection, face recognition, weapon detection, crowd analytics. (6) Sign Language Recognizer — ML model with MPU6050 sensors and Kalman filters for gesture classification. (7) Gagan Kavach — deep learning model on Jetson Nano for aerial threat detection.

test_cases.query: What events does the robotics club organize?
test_cases.expected_answer: The robotics club organizes major events including Botrush and Robomania, which draw participation from over 2000 technocrats. Events include various competitions (Autonomous, Combat types), workshops, and technical showcases. Events are tagged as upcoming or past based on their dates.
test_cases.grounding_source: MongoDB events collection, Pragati 2024 introduction, events API

test_cases.query: Are there any upcoming events I can participate in?
test_cases.expected_answer: The agent should query the events API which computes status dynamically — events with endDate >= now or startDate >= now (if no endDate) are 'upcoming'. The response lists upcoming events with their competitions, registration status, dates, and locations. If no upcoming events exist, it should say so clearly.

test_cases.query: What competitions were held under Botrush?
test_cases.expected_answer: Botrush is one of the major annual events organized by the Robotics Club. It features multiple competitions of different types (Autonomous, Combat, etc.) with team registrations. Each competition has defined team sizes (min/max), rules, and registration periods. The events API returns competitions populated with full details including title, type, description, team size limits, and rules.
test_cases.grounding_source: MongoDB events + competitions collections, Pragati magazines

test_cases.query: What teams am I part of?
test_cases.expected_answer: The agent should fetch all teams for the authenticated user, showing team name, team code, competition name, approval status (draft/submitted/approved/rejected), member list with names and emails, and whether the user is the leader. If the user is not on any teams, it should state that clearly.

test_cases.query: What's the status of my team's registration? Has it been approved?
test_cases.expected_answer: The agent should retrieve the user's teams and report the approvalStatus for each. Possible states: 'draft' (still editable, not submitted), 'submitted' (locked, waiting admin review), 'approved' (terminal, participation confirmed), 'rejected' (admin declined with a reason, can be edited and resubmitted). If rejected, the rejectedReason should be shown.

test_cases.query: Show me my profile details
test_cases.expected_answer: The agent should return the user's profile including: name, email, department/branch, phone, roll number (if MNNIT), college (if non-MNNIT), whether MNNIT student (isMnnit), profile completion status (isProfileComplete), profile image, bio, codename, and creation date.

test_cases.query: Do I need coding experience to join the club?
test_cases.expected_answer: No, prior coding experience is not required. The club welcomes students from all skill levels. The onboarding program covers everything from basic electronics to ROS 2, and many of the strongest members started with zero robotics experience. You'll be contributing to real projects within weeks.

test_cases.query: Can non-CSE students join the robotics club?
test_cases.expected_answer: Absolutely. Robotics is inherently multidisciplinary — the club needs mechanical engineers for chassis design, CS students for software, ECE for circuits, and even civil/chemical engineers have contributed to specialized projects. Every branch brings a unique perspective. Students from any branch are welcome.

test_cases.query: Does the club give components for projects?
test_cases.expected_answer: Yes, the club maintains a well-stocked inventory of microcontrollers, sensors, motors, 3D-printed parts, and development boards. For competition projects, all materials are provided. Members can also request components for personal projects through the resource allocation system.

test_cases.query: What is the robotics club about? Tell me about the club.
test_cases.expected_answer: Robotics Club MNNIT is a dynamic ecosystem of innovators operating under the Student Activity Centre (SAC) at MNNIT Allahabad, Prayagraj. Established in 2016, they bridge the gap between software intelligence and hardware reality. The club has shipped 50+ projects. Core competencies include Computer Vision, ROS & Simulation, Embedded Systems, CAD & Design, Machine Learning, and Kinematics. Their motto is 'Innovate Automate Dominate'.

test_cases.query: How is the club structured? What are the teams/verticals?
test_cases.expected_answer: The club has five technical verticals: Software, Electronics, Mechanical, Computer Vision, and CAD & Fabrication — each led by a team lead. It is coordinated by a President, Vice President, and Technical Head, with guidance from two faculty advisors. Core competency areas include Computer Vision, ROS & Simulation, Embedded Systems, CAD & Design, Machine Learning, and Kinematics.

test_cases.query: What tech domains does the club work in?
test_cases.expected_answer: The club works across 11 major tech domains: AI/ML (neural networks, autonomous decision making), Aerial Robots (swarm intelligence, UAVs), ROS (robotic communication backbone), Image Processing (computer vision, real-time tracking), Underwater Robots (AUVs), Path Planning & SLAM (localization in unknown environments), Electronics (PCB design, power management), 3D Printing & CAD (digital to physical prototyping), Internet of Things, Kinematics & Control (physics of motion and precision), and Simulation Software (Gazebo, Webots).

test_cases.query: Tell me about the Prosthetic Arm project
test_cases.expected_answer: The Prosthetic Arm has gone through two phases. Phase 1 (2024): Used flex sensors on a glove, ESP32 microcontroller, and servo motors to mimic arm movements. Flex sensors detect finger/wrist movements, transmitted wirelessly via WiFi/Bluetooth to ESP32, which drives a 3D-printed prosthetic arm with basic joints. Phase 2 (2025): Advanced version integrating Electromyography (EMG) and MPU6050 sensors for real-time hand/wrist replication. EMG captures forearm electrical activity, IMU detects orientation. Uses bandpass and Kalman filters for signal accuracy. CAD models in SolidWorks, electronics via Arduino IDE. Budget-friendly alternative to commercial prosthetics.

test_cases.query: What is Pragati magazine?
test_cases.expected_answer: Pragati is the annual magazine of the Robotics Club MNNIT Allahabad. Two issues have been published: Issue 01 (2024) subtitled 'A Big Leap to Future' and Issue 02 (2025) subtitled 'The Quantum Leap - Shaping the Future'. The magazine covers summer projects, the Self-Driving Car project, events (Botrush, Robomania), workshops, achievements (E-Yantra IIT Bombay, Techfest IIT Bombay), Global Alumni Convocation, and behind-the-club profiles.
test_cases.grounding_source: Pragati 2024 cover + TOC, Pragati 2025 cover + TOC

test_cases.query: What achievements has the club had at IIT Bombay competitions?
test_cases.expected_answer: The club has participated and achieved recognition at IIT Bombay events including E-Yantra and Techfest (as documented in Pragati magazine achievements section). The website also highlights that MNNIT students developed the first self-driving car prototype (Times of India, Dec 2019), achieved a breakthrough in Prosthetic Arm technology (Dainik Bhaskar, Aug 2021), and deployed a Vision Guided Rover for advanced surveillance (Jagran News, Feb 2023).

test_cases.query: What is the Robotic Dog project?
test_cases.expected_answer: The Robotic Dog is a quadrupedal robot engineered to mimic natural dog movement using Inverse Kinematics and gait programming. It uses 3D-printed PLA components, servo motors, and Arduino-based control systems. Designed in SolidWorks with precision hardware, it uses IK equations and programmed trajectories for coordinated leg movements. Applications include search and rescue operations, educational demonstrations, and security patrols. The design is modular, upgradable, and adaptable.

test_cases.query: What summer projects were done in the 2024-25 academic year?
test_cases.expected_answer: Summer projects in the 2024-25 academic year (from Pragati 2025 magazine) include: AI Music Generator (LSTM neural nets for music composition), Aplytic Resume Analyzer (NLP-powered recruitment tool), Robotic Dog (quadrupedal robot with IK), XY Plotter (CNC-style 2D drawing machine), Sign Language Recognizer (wearable gesture-to-speech system), Swarm Bots (multi-robot coordination in ROS2/Gazebo), Vision-Guided Rover (autonomous navigation with ArUco markers), Prosthetic Arm Phase 2 (EMG + IMU based), Self-Balancing Bike (omniwheel with PID control), 6-DOF Robotic Arm (industrial manipulator), Gagan Kavach (anti-drone defense system), and Hand Gesture-Based Video Game Controller (OpenCV + MediaPipe).

test_cases.query: How much time do I need to commit to the club weekly?
test_cases.expected_answer: Most members spend 6-8 hours per week on club activities, which is a mix of workshops, build sessions, and independent project work. During competition season the pace picks up, but the club is flexible with academic schedules.

test_cases.query: How do I register for a competition?
test_cases.expected_answer: Sign up on the website and join any active competition from the Events page. You can either create a new team (you become leader, get a 6-character team code to share) or join an existing team using their invite code. Teams go through a draft → submitted → approved flow. Once submitted, an admin reviews and approves the team. Teams are formed based on interest and skill mix, with internal selection for national-level competitions.
test_cases.grounding_source: site_content faq, team state machine, participate flow

test_cases.query: What is CART 95?
test_cases.expected_answer: CART 95 is the name of the Robotics Club's autonomous golf cart used in the Self-Driving Car (SDC) project. It underwent a transformative upgrade where the steering system evolved from a chain drive to a gear drive mesh, significantly enhancing automated steering. It features a high-resolution single-turn magnetic encoder with a planetary gear system for precise steering calibration. The SDC project was initiated in 2022 and CART 95 represents the latest generation of the autonomous vehicle.

test_cases.query: What swarm robotics work has the club done?
test_cases.expected_answer: The Swarm Bots project explores decentralized multi-robot coordination using ROS2 and Gazebo simulation. Three autonomous robots are controlled by PID algorithms and navigate using ArUco marker-based localization. Robots are defined in URDF, and their poses (x, y, θ) are calculated in real time using OpenCV. Each bot adjusts its path based on visual marker feedback for precise, collision-free tracing of mathematical figures. Applications include agriculture, warehouse automation, and search-and-rescue missions.

test_cases.query: Are there any projects related to computer vision?
test_cases.expected_answer: Yes, several projects involve computer vision: Smart CCTV Surveillance System (OpenCV for fire/smoke/weapon/face detection), Vision-Guided Rover (ArUco marker detection via OpenCV with Jetson Nano), Defect Product Detection (CNN-based quality inspection), Gagan Kavach (deep learning object detection for anti-drone defense), Hand Gesture-Based Video Game Controller (OpenCV + MediaPipe for gesture recognition), Swarm Bots (ArUco marker localization via OpenCV), and the SDC project (lane detection, semantic segmentation).

test_cases.query: Where is the robotics club located?
test_cases.expected_answer: The Robotics Club is located at the Student Activity Centre (SAC), MNNIT Allahabad (Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology), Prayagraj - 211004.
test_cases.grounding_source: site_content footer section, Pragati magazine covers

test_cases.query: How can I contact the robotics club?
test_cases.expected_answer: You can contact the club via: Instagram (@roboticsclubmnnit), LinkedIn (Robotics Club MNNIT Allahabad), or Email (roboticsclub@mnnit.ac.in). The club is based at the Student Activity Centre, MNNIT Allahabad, Prayagraj.

test_cases.query: I'm a mechanical engineering student interested in robotics but have no coding experience. Is there a place for me and what projects could I work on?
test_cases.expected_answer: Absolutely! The club explicitly welcomes students from all branches — mechanical engineers are needed for chassis design. No coding experience is required; the onboarding covers basics. Mechanical-heavy projects you could contribute to: Robotic Dog (SolidWorks CAD, 3D-printed PLA components, servo mechanisms), XY Plotter (modular frame, 3D-printed parts, NEMA 17 steppers), Prosthetic Arm (3D-printed with joints and linkages), 6-DOF Robotic Arm (SolidWorks CAD, 3D printing, gripper design), Self-Balancing Bike (hardware assembly, frame design), and the SDC project (hardware construction, steering mechanisms). The club's CAD & Fabrication vertical would be your primary home.
test_cases.grounding_source: FAQ items, who-are-we competencies, project descriptions

test_cases.query: What is Gagan Kavach?
test_cases.expected_answer: Gagan Kavach is an innovative automated defense system designed to detect and respond to aerial threats like enemy drones or unauthorized objects. It uses a Jetson Nano powered by a trained deep learning model and OpenCV to detect black-colored objects (simulated drones). When detected, commands are sent to an Arduino which triggers defense mechanisms such as activating servos or buzzers. The system was built entirely from scratch, combining AI vision with real-time actuation. Components include a camera module, servo motors, LEDs, and a custom chassis. It's scalable and can be upgraded for various object types.

test_cases.query: Show me all teams that are waiting for approval
test_cases.expected_answer: The agent should list all teams with approvalStatus='submitted', showing team name, team code, leader name/email, competition name, member count, submission date, and when it was submitted. Admin can then approve or reject each.

test_cases.query: How many teams are in each approval status?
test_cases.expected_answer: The agent should return counts for each approvalStatus: draft (teams still being formed), submitted (awaiting admin review), approved (confirmed participants), rejected (declined, can resubmit). This matches the status count cards on the admin participations page.

test_cases.query: Create a GitHub issue to track the bug where team approval emails are not being sent after admin approves a team

create_issue.title: Bug: Team approval emails not sent after admin approves
create_issue.body:
## Description
When an admin approves a team via the admin participations dashboard, the team status updates correctly in the database but no email notification is sent to the team leader or members.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Submit a team for approval
2. Admin approves the team from /admin/participations
3. Team status changes to 'approved' but no email is received

## Expected Behavior
Team leader and all members should receive an email notification confirming approval.

## Current Behavior
No email is sent. The approval only reflects on the website.

## Technical Context
- Approval flow: `lib/models/team.ts` → `approveTeam()`
- No email integration exists in the approval flow currently
- Gmail tool is available for the agent but not integrated into the approval pipeline

test_cases.expected_answer: Created GitHub issue on krVatsal/robotics-website with title about team approval email bug, detailed reproduction steps referencing the actual approval flow in lib/models/team.ts, and appropriate labels.

test_cases.query: Create an issue for adding dark mode support to the admin dashboard

create_issue.title: Feature: Add dark mode support to admin dashboard
create_issue.body: The admin pages (/admin/*) should support dark mode using the existing CSS custom properties (--bg, --fg, --border, --accent). The main site already supports theme toggling via ThemeToggle component.

test_cases.expected_answer: Created a GitHub issue requesting dark mode for admin dashboard, referencing existing theme infrastructure.

test_cases.query: The events page is showing all events as 'past' even though we have an event next week. Create an issue for this.

create_issue.title: Bug: Events page incorrectly classifies upcoming events as past
create_issue.body:
## Description
All events on the /events page are showing as 'past' regardless of their actual dates.

## Root Cause Analysis
The status computation in `app/api/events/route.ts` compares `startDate`/`endDate` against `new Date()`. Possible issues:
- Events in DB may have dates stored as strings not parsed correctly
- Timezone mismatch between server and stored dates
- Missing startDate/endDate fields defaulting to 'past'

## Current Logic
```js
if (end && end >= now) status = 'upcoming'
else if (start && !end && start >= now) status = 'upcoming'
else status = 'past'
```

## Fix Applied Previously
This was fixed in commit 397a72d by computing status server-side from dates. If recurring, check that event dates are being stored correctly in MongoDB.

test_cases.expected_answer: Created a detailed issue referencing the actual status computation logic in app/api/events/route.ts, the previous fix in commit 397a72d, and possible root causes.

test_cases.query: Show me all open pull requests on the robotics website repo
test_cases.expected_answer: The agent should list all open PRs with title, author, branch, creation date, and review status. If none exist, state that clearly.

test_cases.query: Create a PR from the feature/onboarding branch to main with a description of the Google-only auth changes

create_pr.title: feat: Google-only auth with two-level onboarding
create_pr.head: feature/onboarding
create_pr.body:
## Changes
- Removed manual JWT-based auth (email/password)
- Google Auth is now the only authentication method
- Two-level auth: partial (Google only) → full (profile completed)
- New onboarding page at /onboarding/complete-profile
- Auto-detects @mnnit.ac.in domain for MNNIT students
- Asks for phone, branch, registration number (MNNIT) or college name (others)
- isProfileComplete flag gates access to protected routes

## Files Changed
- Deleted: auth/signup, api/auth/signin, api/auth/signup, forgot-password, reset-password
- New: onboarding/complete-profile page + API route
- Modified: lib/auth-context.tsx, lib/models/user.ts, lib/validation.ts, middleware.ts
- Updated: navbar, hero, signin page, sdc page, team page

test_cases.expected_answer: Created PR with comprehensive description of the auth system changes, listing deleted/new/modified files.

test_cases.query: What drone racing projects does the club have?
test_cases.expected_answer: The club doesn't have a specific drone racing project. However, related work includes: Gagan Kavach (anti-drone defense system using Jetson Nano and deep learning for aerial threat detection), and the Aerial Robots domain (swarm intelligence and UAV flight dynamics) is listed in the tech stack. The agent should NOT hallucinate a drone racing project.

test_cases.query: Show me robotics projects using ROS and also tell me if there are any upcoming events I can join
test_cases.expected_answer: ROS-based projects: SDC/CART 95 (ROS stack for navigation, SLAM, path planning), Cleaner Bot (ROS2 with SLAM Toolbox and Nav2 stack), Swarm Bots (ROS2 and Gazebo simulation). For upcoming events: queries the events API and lists any with future dates. Should handle both intents in a single response.

test_cases.query: What's the weather in Prayagraj today?

test_cases.query: Delete team XYZ123 from the database
test_cases.expected_answer: The agent should refuse this request as a user-role action. Users do not have write tools. The agent should explain that team deletion requires admin access, or if the user is the team leader, they can leave/manage from the profile page UI. It should NOT attempt any write operation.

It CAN send emails to rejected team leaders but should confirm before sending. The agent should suggest using the admin dashboard UI for team deletion.

dimensions.name: tool_selection_accuracy
dimensions.scoring: 1.0 if exact tool set matches, 0.5 if subset/superset, 0.0 if wrong tools. For edge cases where no tool should be called, 1.0 if no tool called, 0.0 if any tool called.
dimensions.description: Did the agent select the correct tool(s) for the query?

dimensions.name: tool_argument_quality
dimensions.scoring: 1.0 if args are optimal (correct filters, scopes), 0.5 if reasonable but suboptimal, 0.0 if wrong args or missing critical params.

dimensions.name: answer_accuracy
dimensions.scoring: Semantic similarity (cosine) between agent answer and expected_answer. >= 0.80 = 1.0, >= 0.60 = 0.5, < 0.60 = 0.0. Key facts must be present.
dimensions.description: Is the answer factually correct and complete?

dimensions.name: hallucination_free
